questions.q: What does Yahweh tell the army of Egypt to do?
questions.a: He tells them to get their shields, horses, spears, and armor ready and go forward to fight.

questions.q: Who are the two kings who are going to have a war?
questions.a: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and Neco king of Egypt were going to war.

questions.q: What does Yahweh see the Egyptian army doing?
questions.a: He sees the Egyptian soldiers running for safety but defeated at the Euphrates River.

questions.q: What does Yahweh compare the Egyptian army to?
questions.a: The army is like the Nile River when it floods and destroys cities and inhabitants.

questions.q: How will Yahweh get his vengeance?
questions.a: He will get his vengeance when the sword devours and is satisfied. That will be like a sacrifice to Yahweh.

questions.q: What does Yahweh tell Egypt to do?
questions.a: They are to go to Gilead for medicine, but it will not cure them.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell the people of Migdol and Memphis to do?
questions.a: He told them to got to Tahpanhes and fight there.

questions.q: What has happened to Egypt’s gods?
questions.a: Apis the bull-god has run away and Yahweh has thrown him down.

questions.q: What do the soldiers want to do?
questions.a: They want to go to their homes.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say Egypt needs to prepare for?
questions.a: He says Egypt needs to prepare for captivity.

questions.q: What animals does the writer say Egypt is like before the battle?
questions.a: Egypt is a beautiful young cow, and the hired soldiers are like a fattened bull.

questions.q: What animal does the writer say Egypt is like after the battle?
questions.a: He says Egypt is like a snake.

questions.q: Who will kill the soldiers of Egypt?
questions.a: People from the north will cut them down.

questions.q: To whom will Yahweh give Egypt?
questions.a: He will give Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do for his people Israel?
questions.a: He will bring them out of captivity, return them to their land where they will find peace and be secure, bring destruction to the nations where they were scattered, discipline them justly, but not destroy them completely.

commentary.text: The defeat of the Egyptians. (Jer. 46:1-12) Their overthrow after the siege of Tyre. (Jer. 46:13-26) A promise of comfort to the Jews. (Jer. 46:27,28)

Jer. 46:1-12 The whole word of God is against those who obey not the gospel of Christ; but it is for those, even of the Gentiles, who turn to Him. The prophecy begins with Egypt. Let them strengthen themselves with all the art and interest they have, yet it shall be all in vain. The wounds God inflicts on his enemies, cannot be healed by medicines. Power and prosperity soon pass from one to another in this changing world.

Jer. 46:13-28 Those who encroached on others, shall now be themselves encroached on. Egypt is now like a very fair heifer, not accustomed to the yoke of subjection; but destruction comes out of the north: the Chaldeans shall come. Comfort and peace are spoken to the Israel of God, designed to encourage them when the judgments of God were abroad among the nations. He will be with them, and only correct them in measure; and will not punish them with everlasting destruction from his presence.
